definition: Concord means a formal state of peace and agreement between parties — harmony with the weight of a treaty behind it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word concord. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know concord should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After the fence settlement, the two farms entered a long concord — gates left unlocked, machinery lent both ways.
A truce stops far short of concord — it only stops the shooting, with the quarrel paused rather than healed, while concord means the parties have grown genuinely easy with each other.
Unity goes further than concord — in concord the parties remain themselves, at peace; in unity the border between them is gone altogether.

Harmony is the everyday word for parts agreeing sweetly — voices in a choir, colors in a room, flavors in a dish — and it needs no history behind it. Concord is grander and more formal: a settled peace between parties who once quarreled, with the ease of people who have genuinely put a fight behind them.

Amity is friendly relations, especially between nations — the diplomatic warmth of allies who simply get along. Concord runs deeper and carries a memory: the parties were once at odds, and the quarrel has healed. Amity never needed a fight; concord is peace after one.
